title: The Elephants and the Mice
text:
A great colony of mice lived in the ruins of an old abandoned town near a lake. A herd of elephants, on their way to drink, began to take a path to the lake that ran straight through the mouse town. Every time the herd passed, huge feet crushed burrows and killed many mice.

The king of the mice went to the king of the elephants and asked politely whether the herd could take a different route. Then he added that if the elephants ever needed help, the mice would remember the favor. The elephant king was amused that such tiny creatures could ever help him, but he agreed and led his herd by another path.

Some time later a king sent trappers to capture elephants. They caught the elephant king and many of his herd in a trap and tied the animals fast with thick ropes to strong trees in the forest. The captive elephant king thought of the mice and sent one of his elephants that had escaped the trap to ask their king for help.

The mice came out in thousands. They swarmed over the ropes and gnawed through every one of them, and the elephants walked free.
lesson: Use your strength considerately, and listen when someone weaker asks for fair treatment. Goodwill you build when you hold the power may save you later.
source: Panchatantra, Book II (The Winning of Friends)
